2:1.sourceText: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἦλθον οὐ καθ’ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:1.targetText: And I, having come to you, brothers, came—not in superiority of discourse or wisdom—declaring to you the testimony of God,

2:2.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον.
2:2.targetText: for I decided not to know anything among you, except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified;

groups.note: Actual τοῦτον is the accusative demonstrative this-one, resuming the immediately named Jesus Christ. LSV renders that same personal demonstrative as Him without changing its original demonstrative morphology into an αὐτός pronoun.

2:3.sourceText: κἀγὼ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ πολλῷ ἐγενόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
2:3.targetText: and I, in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling, was with you;

groups.note: Actual ἐγενόμην is the aorist become/be-in-a-condition form, rendered was in this description; its source remains γίνομαι rather than a written εἰμί form.

2:4.sourceText: καὶ ὁ λόγος μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμά μου οὐκ ἐν πειθοῖς σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀποδείξει Πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως,
2:4.targetText: and my word and my preaching was not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power—

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with my word or my preaching.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula for the word/preaching description. Pinned N1904 has the noun subjects and manner phrases without an independently written be verb.

2:5.sourceText: ἵνα ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν μὴ ᾖ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ.
2:5.targetText: that your faith may not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your faith.

2:6.sourceText: Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις, σοφίαν δὲ οὐ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐδὲ τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τῶν καταργουμένων·
2:6.targetText: And wisdom we speak among the perfect, and wisdom not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age—of those becoming useless,

groups.note: The actual perfect/mature adjective is substantival after the article, rendered the perfect; no separate Greek perfect-people noun is printed.

2:7.sourceText: ἀλλὰ λαλοῦμεν Θεοῦ σοφίαν ἐν μυστηρίῳ, τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην, ἣν προώρισεν ὁ Θεὸς πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς δόξαν ἡμῶν·
2:7.targetText: but we speak the hidden wisdom of God in a secret, that God foreordained before the ages to our glory,

groups.note: Actual ἀποκεκρυμμένην is the perfect passive hidden participle modifying wisdom. English hidden retains that participial form without introducing another independent hiding event.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

2:8.sourceText: ἣν οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἔγνωκεν· εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν Κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν·
2:8.targetText: which no one of the rulers of this age knew, for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of Glory;

groups.note: Actual ἔγνωκεν is perfect indicative, rendered knew in LSV; the original perfect form is retained rather than silently relabeled as a Greek aorist.

2:9.sourceText: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται Ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη, ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
2:9.targetText: but according as it has been written: “What eye did not see, and ear did not hear, and on the heart of man did not come up, what God prepared for those loving Him”;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

2:10.sourceText: ἡμῖν γὰρ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος· τὸ γὰρ Πνεῦμα πάντα ἐραυνᾷ, καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:10.targetText: but God revealed [them] to us through His Spirit, for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God,

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 prints explanatory γάρ, for, after to-us. Pinned CrossWire TR instead prints δέ, matching LSV’s initial but; the differing connective readings remain explicit rather than assigning an adversative sense to this γάρ.
The Greek articles are not separately expressed with God or His Spirit.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has the adversative but, matching the pinned TR δέ reading. N1904 instead prints explanatory γάρ at this position.
LSV explicitly adds a personal possessor to Spirit, corroborated by the TR αὐτοῦ reading. Pinned N1904 has the article/Spirit phrase without a written possessive.

English supplies the revelation object referring back to the preceding things description. Pinned N1904 does not independently print an object pronoun with revealed; no extra source pronoun is invented.

2:11.sourceText: τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ; οὕτως καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ἔγνωκεν εἰ μὴ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:11.targetText: for who of men has known the things of the man, except the spirit of the man that [is] in him? So also the things of God no one has known, except the Spirit of God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the relative in-him description. Pinned N1904 has an attributive article and in-him phrase without a written be verb here.

2:12.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν·
2:12.targetText: And we did not receive the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that [is] of God, that we may know the things conferred by God on us,

groups.note: Actual ἐκ marks the Spirit’s out-of/from-God relation, rendered of in this English qualifier. Its source remains the printed preposition rather than a genitive article.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God in the by-God agent phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the Spirit-that-is-of-God qualifier; the source has an attributive article and out-of-God phrase without a written be verb.

2:13.sourceText: ἃ καὶ λαλοῦμεν οὐκ ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐν διδακτοῖς Πνεύματος, πνευματικοῖς πνευματικὰ συνκρίνοντες.
2:13.targetText: which things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Holy Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things,

groups.note: Actual διδακτοῖς is the verbal adjective taught, used here with the understood words from the preceding contrast. English those taught realizes the substantive adjective construction without an independently printed those pronoun.
The actual genitive Spirit expresses the source/agent of the taught words, rendered by the Spirit; no separate Greek by preposition is printed in this phrase.

Actual πνευματικοῖς is dative plural spiritual, whose masculine/neuter endings coincide. LSV renders the substantive adjective with spiritual things; the printed source supplies neither a separate things noun nor an unambiguous noun gender.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly qualifies Spirit as Holy, matching the longer TR wording; pinned N1904 has Spirit without a written Holy adjective here.

2:14.sourceText: ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Θεοῦ· μωρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστίν, καὶ οὐ δύναται γνῶναι, ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται.
2:14.targetText: and the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he is not able to know [them], because they are discerned spiritually;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the knowing object referring to the preceding things. The actual infinitive know has no independently written object pronoun at this position.

2:15.sourceText: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει μὲν πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ’ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται.
2:15.targetText: and he who is spiritual, indeed discerns all things, and he himself is discerned by no one;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relative copula in he who is spiritual. The source has substantive article and spiritual adjective without a written be verb at this position.

2:16.sourceText: τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου, ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν; ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν Χριστοῦ ἔχομεν.
2:16.targetText: for who knew the mind of the LORD that he will instruct Him? And we have the mind of Christ.

groups.note: Actual ὃς is the masculine relative who, referring to the interrogated person able to instruct. English uses that to introduce the same relative clause; it is not relabeled as a Greek purpose conjunction.
